<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `efbe0361a9f3d8035d176162219787f31ffb4eef` — the merge of head `d0a1903b777dd1cfb6821eac4872e3a6287e91ee` into base `4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin efbe0361a9f3d8035d176162219787f31ffb4eef && git checkout efbe0361a9f3d8035d176162219787f31ffb4eef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 d0a1903b777dd1cfb6821eac4872e3a6287e91ee && git checkout -B drift-repro 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 && git merge --no-ff d0a1903b777dd1cfb6821eac4872e3a6287e91ee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d0a1903b777dd1cfb6821eac4872e3a6287e91ee`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-02T02:56Z by an isolated reviewer (a subagent of the dispatching seat's session, below), read-only: the net diff `origin/main...d0a1903b7` (merge-base `d2bc644f2`, 16 files, +692/−18), card #21260 with every comment (ruling `5942331027` on #21175 included), PR #21296's body and file list, and the check-runs on the head. Files at the head were read with `git show`; nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run. Security family: classes and positions only, no stored values.

**Check-runs on the head.** The seven required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — all conclude `success`; no check-run on the head concludes `failure` (the only non-success conclusions are `skipped` opt-in/duplicate-trigger jobs). The PR's own checks (`Check Changeset`, card-claims-branch, single-writer path, part-of) are `success`. Governed surfaces: none of the 16 paths is `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. Head repo = base repo. 710 changed lines, under the 5,000 human-merge bound. Draft, base `main`. Commits carry the model-free trailer pair and no model identifier.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` gains one entry** (`view_all_audit_log`, label "View All Audit Log", `scope: 'org'`), so `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_NAMES` widens by one. Each implied consequence, judged:
   - the curated seeder (`bootstrapSystemCapabilities`) seeds one more `managed_by: 'platform'` `sys_capability` row; no generated artifact moves (a constant, not a Zod key) — the dev's `check:generated` read "up to date" and the green `TypeScript Type Check` job is where those gates run. **Right.**
   - the authoring accept-set widens: `validateCapabilityReferences` now resolves a `requiredPermissions` / `systemPermissions` reference to the name. This is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` arm. **Right.**
   - the anchor floor needs no edit: `high-privilege.ts` excuses app-declared names only outside `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_NAMES`, so a set carrying the capability is refused on `everyone` and on `guest` even when an app declares the same name — pinned in `high-privilege.test.ts`. **Right.**
   - the mirror consequence: an app declaration of the same name is refused by `bootstrap-declared-capabilities` (curated names are platform-owned). That is the standing reservation rule applied to one more name, as for every curated addition before it; it is not a Clause-② narrowing arm. No hand-kept copy of the curated list exists outside spec that would owe a row: `permission-metadata.mdx:177` is an illustrative sample carrying non-curated names, `permission-sets.mdx:151` is a non-exhaustive "such as", the liveness ledger is keyed by property (`systemPermissions`), and no i18n bundle carries capability labels. **Right.**
   - `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ONLY_CAPABILITIES` (plugin-security) is untouched, so holding the capability confers no `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung and no Layer-0 exemption — correct for an org-scoped grant, and the PR body says so. **Right.**
2. **`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES.systemPermissions` gains the entry**, so platform administrators hold it by default through both anchors: the grant anchor (`admin_full_access`, which plugin-security's `default-permission-sets.ts` spreads from this constant) and the config anchor (`resolve-authz-context.ts` §6b-config pushes the constant's list onto a configured owner). No role-name test anywhere. The exact-list pin in plugin-security is updated on purpose with a docblock saying why, and a new pin holds that no other shipped set carries it. **Right.** Upgrade reading, for the changeset's "Migration: None": the shipped declaration is re-seeded on every boot (the package door's own-row re-seed; `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` seeds the platform bucket on every boot), so an existing deployment's grant-anchored administrators hold it at the first boot after upgrade and a config-anchored owner reads the constant directly; the two pre-existing drift classes (`overlay_shadow`, `provenance_skip`) are surfaced by `permission-set-drift.ts` and apply to this capability exactly as they did to `manage_sharing`. **Right.**
3. **The exemption is the shared mechanism's and nothing else's.** `ParentRecordGate` gains one optional field, `exemptCapability`; `computeParentRecordFilter` gains step 0, decided before the pre-scan and returning `null`, so nothing is ANDed in and the caller's own `where` is untouched (pinned: the returned `where` is the caller's object, no scan, no probe, on find/findOne/count/aggregate). "Held" is `Array.isArray(context.systemPermissions)` and membership: an absent set, a non-list, or a different capability leaves the gate unchanged (pinned) — fail closed. The system-context skip is unchanged. Only `LEDGER_GATE` declares the field; `ACTIVITY_GATE` declares none and its docblock says so, so a holder is narrowed on `sys_activity` exactly as any caller — pinned at unit, integration (real SQLite) and dogfood. This matches the ruling's "the ledger" and the card's "no per-door copy". **Right.** Public surface: neither `ParentRecordGate` nor `LEDGER_AUDIT_CAPABILITY` is exported from plugin-audit's index, so the package's published API is unchanged while its behaviour widens. **Right** (see ②).
4. **What still applies to a holder.** Object-level read on `sys_audit_log` (the gate is a read seam on an object the caller already reaches); the field redaction (`audit-log-field-redaction.ts`, a separate seam reading `resolveServedFields`, where a parent object the service cannot answer masking for serves no field — fail closed); and the tenant wall. Pinned on a real boot: a withheld field's value is absent from the deleted record's served snapshot and present at rest, and under a walled two-organization boot the holder is served its own organization's deleted-record rows (2) and none of the other's (0), the non-holder 0 and 0, the platform administrator 2 and 2 through its own wall bypass. **Right.**
5. **`scope: 'org'`** (the dispatch default was `platform` unless measured): at runtime `scope` is declarative — consumed by the `sys_capability` row seed and by the meta-write predicate's own check only — and the organization bound is the tenant wall's, which this capability does not lift. The declaration states what the runtime does; under `single` posture one organization is every row, consistent. **Right.**
6. **Docs and corrected pins.** The one ledger-reader sentence (`record-view-auditing.mdx:209-218`) now names the capability, the default holder, the field narrowing and the organization bound, and matches 3–5 above. The two #21194 pins the ruling makes false are corrected rather than deleted (the reader is still served none of the deleted record's rows; the administrator, now a default holder, is served both). **Right.**
7. **Breadth, stated not hidden:** a holder is served rows about records of objects it holds no object-level read on, snapshots field-narrowed. That is what "exempt from the parent-record gate" means in the ruling; the capability's description and the docs page both say it. **Right.**

No derived judgment is wrong. Nothing in the diff advertises a capability the runtime does not deliver: every claim in the PR body's pin table has a test at the head, and the dev's three ablation legs (exemption removed, exemption on the activity gate, capability held by everyone) each went red as predicted — the dev's evidence, not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/21260-ledger-audit-capability.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — one arm, the same line as the PR body's line 2 and the claim. `yes` takes at least `minor`: satisfied. The change is additive (a new curated entry, a new optional gate field, no removal and no rename), so it is not breaking and no ADR-0087 marker is owed; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. **Matches the diff.**
- Published surface: spec gains no new export (`check:api-surface` runs in the green type-check job); plugin-audit's index exports nothing new. Behaviour widens in both packages, so `minor` is the right level and `patch` would be wrong. **Matches.**
- Note, not a finding: plugin-security and core change behaviour only through the spec declaration they spread or read; both sit in the changeset `fixed` group, so their versions move with spec regardless, and the CHANGELOG sentence lands in spec and plugin-audit, the two packages whose source changed. Acceptable.
- The changeset's five bullets and its Migration paragraph were re-checked sentence by sentence against the diff and the readings above; each holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report `5944449119`, its `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`) and the item the seat carried to this review, each answered:

1. **`eval-user.zod.ts` edited before being reported** — the claim ordered "report before touching" for a grant path outside plugin-security. A deviation from the claim's order, recorded and accepted by the seat in revision `5944486484`, with the cross-lane declaration on the spec seat post. The edit is the one line the ruling's default holder needs, in the `domain:spec` lane the claim already declared under `Clause-②: yes`. Answered: accepted; no escalation.
2. **Scope `org` instead of `platform`** — judged right in ①-5; the armed check and the pins assert `org`. Answered.
3. **`origin/main` not merged before opening the PR (§10)** — the upstream commits since the merge-base touch none of the 16 paths; the head's check-runs are green and the queue rebuilds the merge ref (§7). Answered: accepted.
4. **Item-1 base reading measured with the exemption line removed rather than at the base dist** — a measurement-order caveat on the pre-change reading only; the verdict rests on the pins at the head. Answered: no bearing.
5. **Ablation leg B's first run was a refused no-op and was re-run** — the readings cited are the re-run's. Answered: no bearing.
6. **Agent principals (ADR-0090 D10)**, carried by the seat: the exemption reads the resolved `systemPermissions`; an OAuth agent principal carries its delegator's set only under `actions:execute` consent and none otherwise (`assemble-execution-context.ts`), and its object-level read on `sys_audit_log` is still judged on its scope-derived ceiling intersected with the user's. So an agent is served the trail only when its delegator holds the capability (by default or by explicit grant), the user consented, and the agent's ceiling reaches the ledger — it is a delegate of a holder, not a position holding anything of its own, which is what the ruling's "every other position gets it only by explicit grant" speaks to. Two pre-existing data-plane reads key on the same set the same way (`sys_record_share` self-scope in plugin-sharing; the object-schema mask exemption in metadata-core). Judged consistent with the ruling; not a defect. One note for the seat, not filed by this review: the comment in `assemble-execution-context.ts` saying cap-gated OBJECT access stays denied to the agent "regardless of this line" predates the sharing read scope and now has a third counter-example; a comment-accuracy debt older than this PR.
7. **`open_questions`**: none declared; none found.
